Read input files RNA

The raw data was procesesd using nf-core/metatdenovo (v1.0.1): https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/1.0.1/ using Prokka as orf caller, GTDB release 220 for taxonomic annotation, and EggNOG mapper for functional annotation.

Expand code 
gtdb <- read_tsv("data/metatdenovo/user_assembly.prokka.gtdb-r220.diamond.taxonomy.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>%
  select(-strain,-taxonomy) %>%
  filter(!is.na(phylum))

# The GTDB metadata 'md' is to join the NCBI with the GTDB taxonomy
pro <- read_tsv("data/metatdenovo/user_assembly.prokka.ncbi-refseq-20250115.diamond.taxonomy-taxdump.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>%
  filter(superkingdom %in% c("Bacteria", "Archaea")) %>%
  select(orf, evalue, taxid) %>%
  filter(!orf %in% gtdb$orf) 

md <- read_tsv("./data/magmap/ar53_metadata_r226.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F)
md <- read_tsv("./data/magmap/bac120_metadata_r226.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>% rbind(md)

pro <- md %>% 
  filter(gtdb_representative) %>%
  select(taxid = ncbi_taxid, gtdb_taxonomy) %>%
  filter(taxid %in% pro$taxid) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(gtdb_taxonomy, delim = ";", names = c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")) %>%
  mutate(species = NA) %>%
  mutate(across(-1, \(x) gsub(x, pattern = "[a-z]__", replacement = ""))) %>%
  mutate(genus = gsub("_[A-Z]", "", genus)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(taxid) %>% slice_sample(n = 1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  inner_join(pro, ., by = "taxid")

euk <- read_tsv("data/metatdenovo/user_assembly.prokka.ncbi-refseq-20250115.diamond.taxonomy-taxdump.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>%
  filter(superkingdom == "Eukaryota" | superkingdom == "Viruses") %>%
  select(-taxonomy) %>%
  select(orf, taxid, evalue, domain = superkingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species)

# Identify ORFs that are identified as prokaryotes with GTDB but eukaryotes according to NCBI
orfs <- gtdb %>%
  select(orf, gtdb.evalue = evalue) %>%
  inner_join(euk, by = "orf") %>%
  filter(evalue > gtdb.evalue) %>%
  pull(orf)

# Merge into one object: 
tax <- gtdb %>%
  filter(!orf %in% orfs) %>%
  rbind(pro) %>%
  rbind(euk %>% filter(!orf %in% gtdb$orf))

remove(md, orfs, pro)
Expand code 
tpm <- read_tsv("data/metatdenovo/user_assembly.prokka.counts.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>% 
  mutate(sample = gsub("R", ".", sample)) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
    "S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2", "S3.1", "S3.2", "S4.1", "S4.2", "S5.1", "S6.1", 
    "S5.2", "S6.2", "S7.1", "S7.2", "S8.1", "S8.2", "S9.1", "S9.2", "S10.1", "S10.2"
  ))) %>%
  select(-start, -end,- strand, -length, -chr)

meta <- read_tsv("data/metatdenovo/sample_key.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(station = as.character(station)) %>%
  mutate(sample = gsub("R", ".", sample)) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
    "S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2", "S3.1", "S3.2", "S4.1", "S4.2", "S5.1", "S6.1", 
    "S5.2", "S6.2", "S7.1", "S7.2", "S8.1", "S8.2", "S9.1", "S9.2", "S10.1", "S10.2"
  ))) %>%
  mutate(layer = factor(layer, levels = c("10m", "chlMax")))

In total, there are 20 metatranscriptomes from five stations. At every station, samples were taken in duplicates from 10 m depth and from chl. max. On average, each sample has 81.2 million reads (sd 8.7, n = 20). Off all the transcripts, 53.0 % was functionally annotated (Eggnog mapper), 36.5 % was functionally annotated including a KO reference, 45.7 % of the transcripts was annotated on phylum level, 45.7 % on order level, 44.8 % on genus level, and 32.7 % on species level.

25.2 % of the transcript were functionally annotated with Prokka. A summary of the bioinformatic pipeline will soon be added to this introduction.

Expand code 
eggnog <- read_tsv("data/metatdenovo/user_assembly.prokka.emapper.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>%
  mutate(kegg_ko = gsub("ko:", "", kegg_ko)) %>%
  filter(kegg_ko != "-") %>%
  select(orf, evalue, cog = cog_category, ko = kegg_ko, module = kegg_module, name = preferred_name, description, max_annot_lvl)

Read input files DNA

Forward primer 515F (5’ GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA), reverse primer 926R (5’ CCGYCAATTYMTTTRAGTTT) from Parada et al. (2015) [1]. The data was submitted to ENA under the reference PRJEB63557.

Expand code 
read_delim("data/ampliseq/params.yaml", delim = " ", col_names = c("parameter", "value"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  knitr::kable()

project: naiss2024-5-56
input: samples.tsv
outdir: output
FW_primer: GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA
RV_primer: CCGYCAATTYMTTTRAGTTT
trunclenf: 269
trunclenr: 209
double_primer: true
sample_inference: independent
dada_ref_taxonomy: sbdi-gtdb
skip_qiime: true

  pivot_longer(-1, names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>% mutate(sample = gsub("_S..", "", sample)) %>%
  rename(seqid = ASV_ID) %>%
  group_by(sample) %>% mutate(relab = count / sum(count)) %>% ungroup()
  
asv <- read_tsv("data/ampliseq/ASV_tax_species.sbdi-gtdb.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename(seqid = ASV_ID) %>% rename_with(tolower) %>% select(-species_exact, -confidence, -sequence)

Data exploration

Rarefaction

Expand code 
# The lowest number of reads in a sample is 4.1 million

rare <- tpm %>%
  select(-tpm) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "orf", values_from = "count", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample") %>%
  vegan::rarecurve(sample = 4.1e6, step = 1e5, tidy = TRUE) %>%
  tibble() %>%
  rename_with(tolower)
Expand code 
rare %>%
  rename(samplesize = sample, sample = site, n.orfs = species) %>%
  inner_join(meta, by = "sample") %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = samplesize, 
    y = n.orfs,
    colour = layer
    )) + 
  geom_line() + scale_color_manual(
    values = c("10m" = "#899DA4", "chlMax" = "#046C9A"),
    labels = c("10m" = "10 m", "chlMax" = "Chl. max")
    ) +
  labs(x = "No. of sequence reads", y = "Rarefied No. of ORFs") +
  #scale_x_continuous(labels = c("0", "50.000", "100.000", "150.000")) +
  theme_tidy(fontsize = 6) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.85, 0.15)
  )

Percentage of annotated transcripts

Expand code 
i <- c("domain","phylum","class","order","family","genus")

for (level in i) {
  ## The (!!as.name(level)) converts the variable level to e.g. 'genus'
  d <- tpm %>% left_join(tax, by = "orf") %>% filter(!is.na((!!as.name(level))))
  format(nrow(d) / nrow(tpm) * 100, digits = 3) %>% paste(stringr::str_to_title(level), ": ", ., " %", sep = "") %>% print()
}

Community composition on domain level

Expand code 
tpm %>%
  left_join(tax, by = "orf") %>%
  replace_na(list("domain" = "Unknown")) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>% summarise(tpm = sum(tpm) / 20, .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(tpm))

Figure 2 depicts the ratio between bacteria and archaea for both depth layers. Note how the abundance of archaea is slightly higher in most of the deeper samples (chlorophyll max depth).

Community composition

Community composition - phylum

Expand code 
t <- tpm %>%
  inner_join(gtdb, by = "orf") %>%
  group_by(phylum, sample) %>%
  # Sum the abundance of each phylum within a sample
  summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = 'drop_last') %>%
  # Calculate the mean abundance of each phylum over the categories
  summarise(mean.tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(!is.na(phylum)) %>%
  top_n(8, mean.tpm)

t %>% arrange(desc(mean.tpm))
# A tibble: 8 × 2
  phylum           mean.tpm
  <chr>               <dbl>
1 Pseudomonadota   4808857.
2 Thermoplasmatota 1203895.
3 Bacteroidota      837256.
4 Cyanobacteriota   605384.
5 Thermoproteota    550623.
6 Marinisomatota    227683.
7 Chloroflexota     207959.
8 SAR324            150061.

Figure 3 explores the data by plotting the most abundant phyla over all samples, regardless if the RNA transcript was functionally annotated or not. Note that the taxonomy is outdated and needs to be updated (e.g. Pseudomonadota instead of Proteobacteria). 87.7 % of the annotated ORFs are affiliated with bacteria, while 13.1 % is affiliated with Archaea.

Community composition - genus

Expand code 
t <- tpm %>%
  inner_join(tax, by = "orf") %>% filter(domain %in% c("Bacteria", "Archaea")) %>%
  group_by(genus, sample) %>%
  # Sum the abundance of each phylum within a sample
  summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = 'drop_last') %>%
  # Calculate the mean abundance of each phylum over the categories
  summarise(mean.tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(!is.na(genus)) %>%
  top_n(10, mean.tpm)

t %>% left_join(tax, by = "genus") %>% 
  select(genus, order, phylum, mean.tpm) %>% 
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(desc(mean.tpm)) %>%
  rename(Genus = genus, Order = order, Phylum = phylum) %>%
  knitr::kable()

Figure 5 shows the most abundant genera. It reveals how some genera (e.g. Pelagibacter and Ketobacter) are more abundant (and active) in the 10 m depth, while for example Nitrosopumilus is more abundant in the deeper sites. Note from the metadata that the depth of chlorophyll max strongly varies between the stations.

The gene list is from Royo-Llonch et al. [2]. It contains the KEGG ortholog (KO) and the pathway the gene is involved in. KOs of interest in the data that are not represented in the gene list are manually categorized. Shows the RNA transcripts for the carbon fixation pathways for each depth layer. To do so, one KO catalyzing the rate-limiting reaction was selected for each pathway. The Wood-Ljungdahl pathway was also included in this analysis but the representing KO was not detected, or the detected KO did not have a taxonomic annotation.

p5

Figure 8 shows the tpm for each representative KO summed over all the samples (n = 20). N transformation, central C metabolism, and photosynthesis plus aerobic respiration. Udh uronate dehydrogenase, edd phosphogluconate dehydratase, icd isocitrate dehydrogenase, ICL isocitrate lyase, G6PD glucose-6-phosphate 1-dehydrogenase, PRPP phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate, RPPK ribose-phosphate pyrophosphokinase, ED: Entner–Doudoroff. Note how the transcripts involved in carbon fixation are predominantly represented by the Streptomycetales (Streptomyces sp.) and the Burkholderiales (Nitrosomonas sp.) while only few transcripts were detected affiliated with cyanobacteria. The oxidation from ammonia to nitrite (nitrification) is performed by Nitrosopumilus sp. while the further oxidation from nitrite to nitrate (K00370) is done by a representative from the family Nitrospinaceae.

Differential gene expression using edgeR

This analysis helps to identify differentially expressed genes between the 10 m depth and the chlorophyll max depth. Station 5 is not included in the analysis as it introduces too much noise.

Expand code 
library(edgeR)
Loading required package: limma
Expand code 
i <- meta %>% filter(!station %in% c("5", "56")) %>% pull(sample)

m <- tpm %>%
  filter(sample %in% i) %>% # Leave out station 5 for the moment
  select(-tpm) %>%
  arrange(sample) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = "count", names_from = "sample", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("orf") # Create a numeric matrix

dge <- tpm %>%
  filter(sample %in% i) %>% # Leave out station 5 for the moment
  select(-tpm) %>%
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "orf") %>% separate_longer_delim(ko, delim = ",") %>%
  group_by(sample, ko) %>% summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(sample) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = "count", names_from = "sample", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("ko") %>%
  DGEList(group = meta %>% filter(sample %in% i) %>% pull(layer), lib.size = colSums(m))

The chunk below is to create the design matrix, make the contract, and run the actual analysis using the functions glmQLfit() and glmQLFTest()

Expand code 
design.mat <- model.matrix(~ 0 + meta %>% filter(sample %in% i) %>% arrange(sample) %>% pull(layer))
rownames(design.mat) <- colnames(m)
colnames(design.mat) <- c("shallow", "deep")
contrast <- makeContrasts(layer = shallow-deep, levels = design.mat)

dge <- dge %>%
  calcNormFactors() %>%
  estimateDisp(design.mat) %>%
  glmQLFit(design.mat, robust = TRUE)

qlf <- glmQLFTest(dge, contrast = contrast)

The p-values are adjusted according to the false discovery rate, and the DE genes are joined with the functional and taxonomic annotation.

Expand code 
de <- topTags(qlf, adjust.method = "fdr", n = Inf) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("ko") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(expression = case_when(
    fdr < 0.05 & logfc > 0 ~ "up",
    fdr < 0.05 & logfc < 0 ~ "down",
    .default = "non-de"
  )) %>%
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "ko") %>%
  filter(expression != "non-de") %>% tibble()

remove(m, dge, qlf, contrast, design.mat)

As the contrast was shallow vs deep, upregulated means significantly higher in the shallow samples while downregulated means higher in the deeper samples. There are 677 KOs up regulated and 906 KOs down regulated. 0 KOs were not differential expressed.

The 25 KOs with the lowest (up in deeper samples) and 25 with the highest log fold-change are selected. Six of these KOs are represented in the gene list, the other 19 will be manually categorized. The number of 25 was arbitrary chosen. Many of these KOs are affiliated with the archaeon Nitrosopumilus that oxidizes ammonium and is capable of autotrophic growth using the hydroxypropionate/hydroxybutyrate cycle that is more energy efficient than other aerobic C fixation pathways, including the Calvin cycle (source: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1402028111). The fact that C fixation KOs affiliated with this genus are abundantly detected strongly suggests autotrophic growth, possibly due to a low concentration of organic carbon.

m <- seqtab %>% # Standard Vegan transformation
  select(-relab) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = "count", names_from = "seqid", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample") 

adiv <- m %>%
  vegan::diversity() %>% data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample") %>% rename(shannon = ".")
  
adiv <- m %>%
  vegan::specnumber() %>% data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample") %>% rename(specno = ".") %>%
  inner_join(adiv, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(pielou = shannon / log(specno)) %>%
  inner_join(dnakey, by = "sample")
Expand code 
p1 <- adiv %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = layer,
    y = pielou
  )) + 
  geom_boxplot() + labs(y = "Shannon diversity") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("10 m", "Chl. max"))
